## The obligation to carry out God's prescribed punishments

**God Most High says: {And the thief, male and female — cut off their hands} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:38). Is the imperative here for obligation? And if the answer is yes, who is responsible for it, and do the rest sin if they do not command him to do it?**

The imperative is for obligation, and this is one of God's prescribed punishments (ḥadd), which God Most High has made obligatory upon His servants. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «One prescribed punishment carried out on the earth is better for its people than that they should be rained upon for a sabt» — that is, a full week. And in one transmission: «than that they should be rained upon for a month.» You know people's need for rain, and you know its benefit to the earth, its cleansing of the air and its reviving of the dead land; and yet one prescribed punishment carried out on the earth is better for its people than that they should be rained upon for a month.

Suspending a prescribed punishment — suspending any of God's prescribed punishments — is setting oneself against God in His dominion, as in the report of Usamah ibn Zayd, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «Whoever's intercession stands in the way of one of God's prescribed punishments has set himself against God in His dominion.» Therefore it is obligatory (wājib) upon those in authority — upon everyone to whom God has given charge of an affair of the Muslims — to carry out God's prescribed punishments, glorified and exalted is He, and to discharge them in the correct manner.

And we too, the body of the Muslim people, must know that cutting off the thief's hand is not aggression, nor injustice, nor is it cruelty; for no one is more merciful than the Most Merciful of those who show mercy, who created the human being and created for him two hands, two eyes and two ears. He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy, and He is the one who prescribed this punishment, and He is the one who placed the remedy within it. Many people suppose that applying Islam means the cutting off of hands and feet, as some people claim; but the reality is that it is unbelief that today cuts off hands and feet and all the limbs. Do you not see the houses levelled upon their inhabitants in Palestine, Iraq, Afghanistan and elsewhere? Is that not a cutting off of heads and of all the limbs? And yet they claim that human rights are the contrary of this. Therefore we must not be taken in by this tendentious propaganda, and must know that those who promote it are deluded by the unbelievers and give their allegiance to them; and so what they say cannot be accepted from them.

And if God's prescribed punishments are not carried out, this is setting oneself against God on His earth; and setting oneself against God means enmity towards Him. If the people of the earth show enmity to God, they do not harm God, and He has power over them; how slight are the earth and its people in God's sight when they disobey Him. And all people are sinful if they do not demand that God's prescribed punishments be carried out, and if they do not summon every ruler, and everyone who has taken charge of an affair of the Muslims, to carry out God's prescribed punishments and to observe them, and to establish the whole of God's law. So it is obligatory upon the peoples to demand that; and if they fall short in it, they share in the sin with those in authority.

## The ruling on spending from an orphan's property on his brother

**A woman has children, among them some who are mute and deaf and do not hear, and they have a sum of money. Is it permissible for the mother to take their money in order to spend it on their young siblings without their knowledge, and what is the ruling on that?**

We ask God Most High to set their affairs right and to give her joy in them. The answer is that these children's property is theirs, and the maintenance of their siblings is not obligatory upon them. Therefore the mother is not to take from it except what falls under the head of intermixing of households, for God Most High has said: {And if you intermix with them, then they are your brothers} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:220). So she takes from it what she herself needs for her necessary expenses, and spends upon them from it in a fitting way, and tries to make it grow for them; but she is not to spend from it with the aim of using it up, with no return to them and no benefit. For the maintenance of their siblings is not obligatory upon them.

## How to repent from stolen money

**What is the ruling on one who stole a hundred thousand, then repented and wished to return it: does he return it and its profits, or does he return only what he took?**

If a person takes forbidden money and trades with it and makes a profit, the forbidden money is not his, and half the profit likewise is not his — because half the profit follows the capital, whereas the remainder is what follows his own yield, and that is what belongs to him. So he must give up the principal, and must give up half the profit along with it; and he must return it to the one he stole it from; and he must likewise obtain his satisfaction for the period during which he kept him deprived of his money.

## A woman's milk after two years of suckling have passed

**Does a woman's milk, after two years of suckling have passed, create the marriage impediment or not?**

This question is a matter of disagreement among the people of knowledge, and the preponderant view is that it does create it, because milk with its constituents brings about the building up of bone and the growing of flesh, and that is the operative cause (ʿillah) which the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — set out in what Abu Dawud brought out in the Sunan, and others besides him, with a sound chain of transmission: that the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «What builds up the bone and causes the flesh to grow creates the impediment.» And he said: «One suck does not create the impediment, nor two sucks, nor one draught, nor two draughts.»

These two reports are explicit that what is intended is the nourishment of the child, such that his bone and his flesh grow from the woman's milk; and if that comes about, then part of his body arises from part of the woman's body, so that he becomes her son through suckling — by the justice of God, majestic is His majesty. God Most High has said: {Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brothers' daughters, your sisters' daughters, and your mothers who have suckled you} (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:23). He said "your mothers who have suckled you", and did not say "your mothers through suckling", as He said "your sisters through suckling". This is evidence that part of the body grew from her milk, so that she became a mother by it.

Those who hold this adduce in support the story of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri — may God have mercy on him — who is one of the imams of the Successors. His mother used to serve Umm Salamah, Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her. His mother was taken captive in the raid of al-Mawari, in the caliphate of Umar, may God be pleased with him, and his father, who was a client of the Ansar, married her, and she bore al-Hasan. His mother used to serve the Mother of the Believers Umm Salamah, and whenever this child cried Umm Salamah would give him her breast and he would suckle at it, and milk came down from her breast — from the breast of the Mother of the Believers Umm Salamah — in the caliphate of Uthman, after the death of Umar; and al-Hasan used to take pride in having suckled the milk of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan was not born until the last days of Umar, and he did not transmit from him and did not see him; he transmitted from Uthman and Ali and others among the senior Companions.

Al-Badawi — may God have mercy on him — mentioned this story, and al-Dhahabi and others of the great imams mentioned it. Al-Badawi says in his versification of the genealogies:

*And al-Hasan al-Basri is of the descendants of those taken in the raid of al-Mawari; he attained high rank from the breast of Umm Salamah, since his mother was a bondwoman to our Mother.*

## One who drinks his wife's milk

**What is the ruling on one who drank milk that his wife had expressed from her breast without his knowing?**

If he is an adult who has passed the age of suckling, the preponderant view is that this entails neither prohibition nor the spread of the marriage impediment; because if a person drinks, or suckles, after he has completed two years and two months, that does not spread the marriage impediment. For the time of suckling lies within the period God has fixed. God Most High has said: {And his bearing and his weaning are thirty months} (Sūrat al-Aḥqāf 46:15); and He said, exalted is He: {And mothers suckle their children two full years} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:233); and He said, exalted is He: {and his weaning is within two years} (Sūrat Luqmān 31:14). So weaning — which is suckling — is within two years, and what goes beyond that is only by the two completing months; because some of the people of knowledge explained His words, exalted is He, {and mothers suckle their children two full years}, as meaning that "full" is with the addition of two months. So whatever falls outside that does not spread the marriage impediment, according to the position of the majority of the people of knowledge, and according to the preponderant view, God willing.

Some of the people of knowledge held that it spreads it without qualification, and this is what is called the suckling of an adult. Aisha — may God be pleased with her — held that it does spread the marriage impediment, and the Mothers of the Believers differed with her in that. Those who hold this position adduce the report of Sahlah bint Suhayl ibn Amr, who was the wife of Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah — may God be pleased with them both — and they were among the Emigrants. Salim used to lodge with them, and he became known as Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah, though he was the client of a woman of the Ansar. He used to come in upon Sahlah while she was fuḍul, that is, in her sleeping garment only; so she sought a ruling from the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — and he said: «Suckle him.» So she suckled him, and he would come in upon her in that state. Aisha — may God be pleased with her — took the position that the suckling of an adult spreads the marriage impediment; and all the Mothers of the Believers differed with her and held that it does not spread the marriage impediment, and that this was a dispensation (rukhṣah) for Sahlah alone with Salim alone, so that it does not extend beyond its own case, being one of the incidents particular to named individuals.

## Where the imam stands at a funeral prayer

**Where does the imam stand in relation to the bier, whether it is a male or a female?**

The bier of a man was brought to Anas ibn Malik — may God be pleased with him — and he stood opposite his shoulders, that is, opposite his shoulder-blades, and prayed over him. Then a woman was brought, and he stood at her hips and prayed over her. It was said: is this how you saw the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — pray over a man and over a woman? He said: yes, I saw him pray thus. This indicates that in the case of a man the imam stands opposite his upper part, and that in the case of a woman the imam stands opposite her middle. This is the standing position concerning which this report traced to the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — has come; and as for the other views of the jurists, there is no report traced to the Prophet among them. By this it is known that the preponderant view is this position, and that it differs for a man from a woman.

If the imam is praying over two biers, then the man's bier will be the one next to him and the woman's bier after it, because the order — the order of the biers — is that the adult man is next to the imam, then after him the adult woman, then the male child, that is the boy, then after that the female child; in that order. The one next to him is the one whose case determines the ruling. Therefore if a man is next to him, he stands opposite his shoulders, and no weight is given to the biers beyond that.

## Financial funds

**What is the ruling on a women's social financial fund, from which each one of them receives in the case of a marriage or a birth, and in which it is not a condition that the beneficiary be one who pays in?**

If nothing comes back to the woman who pays in, and it is not stipulated that the one who pays in should have the like of what she paid returned to her, then there is no objection to it, because it is part of cooperating in righteousness and God-consciousness. The people of knowledge have mentioned that it is obligatory upon the Muslims to collect money by which the entitlements of the public treasury may be discharged, if the public treasury is not in order. For instance, the obligatory relief of the needy, where there is not enough in the public treasury, or the rulers have laid their hands upon the public treasury and have not disbursed it to its lawful heads of expenditure — then it becomes obligatory upon the Muslims to collect money with which to fill the gap left by the public treasury. Among such things is maintenance for the students of knowledge who study the communal obligations; and among them is the treatment of the sick, maintenance for the needy, the sponsorship of orphans, and other communal obligations (farḍ kifāyah) which are obligatory. So if there is not enough in the public treasury, or there is but it does not reach its heads of expenditure, then it is obligatory upon the Muslims to collect money with which to fill this gap. Among such things are these funds that are purely cooperative and have no commercial character involving exchange for a consideration.

But if each one pays in a thousand, and one of them takes the whole sum this month, then each one pays a thousand and one of them takes the whole sum the next month, and so on — whether this is by drawing lots or by an agreed list — then this is not permissible, because it falls under exchange for a consideration, and it is a loan that has drawn a benefit; for each one paid the thousand in order to take thirty thousand, for example. That will be a loan, and so it falls under a well-known usurious rule, namely "lend to me on condition that I lend to you".

## The time-restricted and the time-extended obligation

**What is the time-restricted obligation and what is the time-extended obligation?**

The obligation (farḍ), among the legal theorists, admits of three divisions. It is divided, with regard to the one who performs it, into the individually obligatory (farḍ ʿayn) and the communally obligatory (farḍ kifāyah). It is divided, with regard to itself, into the specified and the unspecified. And it is divided, with regard to its time, into the time-extended and the time-restricted.

The time-extended is that for which the Lawgiver has appointed a time greater than itself — such as the time of the noon prayer, for instance, which begins from the sun's declining until the shadow becomes the length of a man's height. Within this period four cycles of prayer could be performed a number of times over, so it is wider than the obligation required. The time-restricted obligation is that which the Lawgiver has made to be the measure of the act of worship obliged within it; its time is not exceeded. For instance, fasting the days of the month of Ramadan is a time-restricted obligation, because a person has no alternative to it: if he does not fast this day he is disobedient and in breach, so fasting this particular day is obligatory upon him, if he is free of impediments and fulfils the conditions. So this is the difference between the time-restricted obligation and the time-extended obligation.

## The ruling on masturbation

**Is masturbation by hand, or with a cloth and the like, permissible?**

Masturbation by hand and the like is a matter of disagreement among the people of knowledge, and the reports that have come concerning it are all fabricated (mawḍūʿ) or weak (ḍaʿīf). Some of the people of knowledge held it forbidden, adducing as evidence the words of God Most High: {So whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors (7)} [al-Muʾminūn]. Others held it permissible. And from the two positions there emerges a position that it is disliked (makrūh); it has been transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he gave the ruling that it is disliked, and he said: marrying a slave woman is better than it.

Those who hold it permissible hold that the default is permissibility in whatever no prohibition has come concerning, and that it is the expelling of one of the body's superfluities, like the mucus of the nose and the like. Those who hold it forbidden hold that it is among what is "beyond that", as in the verse of Sūrat al-Muʾminūn. Some of the jurists who hold it permissible have said:

*If you are alone in a valley with no companion in it, then flog Umayrah — there is no sin and no blame.*

The Arabs call that act of masturbation "flogging Umayrah". But this is not sufficient as evidence. Prudence and scrupulousness require that a person take the more cautious side, which is that of prohibition, because God Most High says: {And those who guard their private parts, except from their spouses or those their right hands possess, for then they are not blameworthy; so whoever seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors (7)} [al-Muʾminūn].

flags.note: IMPORTANT, and directly relevant to the glossary. This is a ruling on a rotating savings and credit association — the very structure the style guide uses as its worked example of a flag, under the Mauritanian dialect name 'الكيص'. Here the Sheikh does not use that word, and he distinguishes two structures sharply: a purely cooperative fund, where nothing returns to the contributor, is permissible and indeed meritorious; a rotating fund where each contributor takes the pot in turn is NOT permissible, as a loan that draws a benefit, falling under 'lend to me on condition that I lend to you'. The answer's whole force is in the distinction, so neither half may be quoted alone, and it must not be reported as 'the Sheikh permits savings funds' or 'the Sheikh forbids savings funds'. This answer should be put beside whatever record contains 'الكيص' before that glossary entry is settled.

translator_notes: STRUCTURE. This is not a single fatwa but a compilation of about forty-five separate questions and answers, each with its own heading, run together as one CMS record of roughly 50,000 characters. It has been translated in full, in thirteen passes, with no summarising and nothing skipped; each pass was verified character-for-character against the source before translation, and the reassembled Arabic was verified against the served text as a whole. The English uses a heading for each question and sets the question itself in bold; those are presentational and add no words.

WHAT THIS RECORD IS. An answer inside it refers the reader back to 'the previous episode', and several others say 'we have already mentioned'. This record is therefore a transcription of a serialised broadcast question-and-answer programme, not a set of separately composed written fatwas. Some answers depend on episodes that are not in this record. This matters for the corpus inventory's headline finding that the Sheikh's fatwas exist only as audio: they do, but this record and its companion at ID 672 are substantial written transcriptions of them, and they are not title-only stubs.

SOURCE DEFECTS. Three are structural and are flagged individually: a block of four answers duplicated verbatim within the record; three literal backslashes from an addslashes pass, preserved in body_ar and omitted from body_en; and a Qur'anic quotation that conflates two verses, which the same record quotes correctly elsewhere. Three tatweel padding characters were removed from body_ar as declared normalisation.

QUR'ANIC REFERENCES. The source gives a reference for only a handful of its Qur'anic citations. References have been supplied in the English throughout to meet the house citation format; this is presentation, not restoration, and body_ar is untouched. The single exception is the conflated quotation, which deliberately carries no reference. All Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

HADITH. The Sheikh names a collection or a narrator where he chooses to and not otherwise. No collection, narrator or grading has been added anywhere, and none has been dropped, per style guide section 4.

RULING TERMS. The five-rulings mapping is used strictly, and the weaker formulas the Sheikh often prefers — 'is not permitted', 'there is no objection', 'the matter is not strict', 'prudence requires' — have been kept as weaker formulas and nowhere upgraded to a grading. Several answers turn on precisely that distinction.

EDITORIAL SENSITIVITY. Eight answers carry an editorial_review flag: earning by al-raqīq (unresolved and the most serious), the legally prescribed covering, the prescribed punishments with its political passage, masturbation, the barber's trade, blood money, musical instruments, and the identification of Ibn al-'Arabi.
